## E2 - capture fidelity (edge drops and conservative read windows)

Model, stated plainly: (a) *precise capture with missing edges* drops each
DERIVED_FROM edge independently with probability d (one draw stream per seed, so a
higher rate always drops a superset of the edges); (b) *conservative read-window
capture* gives every write its true parents plus up to K carried-over reads from the
same modelled session (docs/01 section 7.3 "last K READ targets"; 5 actions per
session, which is why the K sweep saturates around 25). E2 is a model of capture
error, not a measurement of real runtime coverage (that is E6, small n).

## E4 - latency (real FalkorDB, real engine calls)

One throwaway graph per size, built through the engine, then the real engine
timed over rounds (the real revoke uses a different root per round, because a
second revoke of the same root is idempotent by design). `build_ms` is the
per-node write path through the engine, not a bulk loader - reported as-is.

## E3 - scenario replay through the HTTP API

`evals/run_e3.py` (also `tests/evals/test_e3_scenarios.py`) POSTs every
authored `demo/scenarios/*.json` node through `/v1/events`, attests the
corroborations with the operator credential, revokes the root through
`/v1/revoke` and asserts the fixture's expected statuses plus a gate probe: the
high-risk push built on the revoked branch is never `allow`. PASS/FAIL only - the
per-scenario expectations live in the fixtures.

`evals/results/e1_samples.csv` (3240 rows), `evals/results/e1_b0_theta_sweep.csv`.

## Limitations (docs/03 section 7, verbatim)

## 7. Honest limitations (paste into README "Limitations")
- Pedigree **contains, explains and reverts**; it does not detect bad sources or prevent prompt injection.
- E1 has built-in ground truth: it quantifies baseline semantics, not lineage discovery. E2 is a model of capture error. E3 replays patterns, not the cited papers' experiments. E6 has small n.
- Session read-window capture over-approximates influence (ratio reported); `cite` edges tighten it but depend on agent cooperation (tagged `agent_reported`).
- `preserved` is only as good as the corroboration signal (explicit independent source asserted by agent/human/scanner).
- Hooks see only what the runtime exposes; paraphrase laundering through an unhooked channel is invisible.
- Bash risk classification is heuristic. External effects (pushes already pulled, emails sent) are listed, not undone.
- Cloud Free: 100 MB, no TLS, no persistence - hosted demo uses synthetic data only; benchmarks ran locally.
- B0-B5 are emulations of semantics described in public docs/papers, not the vendors' products.

## How to reproduce

```bash
make eval          # full grid (N>=30 seeds per cell)
make eval-quick    # one cell, 2 seeds
```
